identity: A scanned, OCR-damaged Arabic multiple-choice exam question bank (بنك أسئلة اختيار من متعدد) for a secondary-school Islamic-education course. 20 items covering آداب الكلام, متطلبات العلوم التطبيقية, السيرة النبوية, صلاح الدين, أركان الصلاة, مجالات البحث العلمي, مهارات الداعية, تعامل النبي مع ذوي الإعاقة, ابن الهيثم, آية ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة, مصنفات القرن الثاني, أم معاوية, عقوبة الجناة, الانتماء للوطن, الشورى, and الفن في الإسلام. The OCR damage proves it is a scan: المجلمر for المجلس, امتالك for امتلاك, طر يق split across two tokens, الاكل and للامام stripped of hamza, الإنتماء. There are 19 <NL> tokens, hence exactly 20 items, one per line-block.
law: This is §J territory: the page furniture IS the sentence. Inside each item the original layout was a question stem terminated by ؟ or :, followed by three to five answer options, each on its own line or in its own cell or behind its own letter label. Every one of those was a unit-ending mark, so every one is a boundary. Consequences: (1) each option is its own segment, however short - one-token segments are licensed by J2; (2) و/أو that merely coordinates nouns inside a single option never cuts (LAW 1 exception, E2 VP-chain); (3) و opening a fresh finite clause with new arguments inside a stimulus passage does cut (LAW 1, C4); (4) a rubric or instruction that FOLLOWS its content welds backward and the cut goes after it (J6, LAW 4), while a lead-in that PRECEDES its content and took a colon splits (J1); (5) trailing عندما / كما / التي adjuncts belong to the clause before them (LAW 4); (6) Arabic بن name-chains never cut (D1 precedent: عن X عن Y inside an isnad link does not cut).
reasoning: REGISTER CALIBRATION FIRST (LAW 6). 533 tokens over 20 items = 26.6 tokens per item. If each item were one sentence I would be sitting at 26 tokens per unit, roughly three times the §J worksheet target of 3-10. Five units per item - stem plus four options - lands at ~4.7 tokens, squarely in band. That arithmetic, plus J2 (each cell its own segment) and LAW 0 (I under-cut 5 to 1), is what commits me to cutting every single option. I place 114 boundaries. || ITEM 1 @7 ميزه. The imperative TRAILS its statement, so by J6/LAW 4 it welds backward and the cut lands after it at @7, not before it at @6 الكلام. Same shape as gold تتميز دولتنا ... أدلل على صحة العبارة ‖. || ITEM 5 @107/@108. The four options can only be قول سمع الله لمن حمده / التشهد الأخير / دعاء الاستفتاح في الصلاة / الوضوء, because في الصلاة precedes الوضوء in token order and therefore cannot belong to it. That leaves الوضوء as a one-token segment, which J2 explicitly licenses (gold وفى ‖ عهده ‖). Med confidence on @107 only. || ITEM 6 is the densest site in the document. The stem carries an embedded example list - الفقه وأصول الفقه / علوم التربية والاجتماع / النفس والاقتصاد / التاريخ / علوم اللغة العربية - before هو, and then only three answer options. الآتية @118 is a colon site (J1: rubric preceding its content splits). Inside the list, note there is no و before النفس @125 and none before التاريخ @127; that missing-waw pattern is the fingerprint of commas in the source, and LAW 0's corollary says those commas became boundaries. I cut them, but at med/lo, because B5 (a comma-set list yields two boundaries, not zero) supports it while I have no §J precedent for a list embedded inside a stem. هو @131 closes the stem rather than opening option A: in this bank هو is consistently the last stem token before the choices - compare @276 and @479. || ITEM 8 @177. The options are garbled OCR but the shape is recoverable: انتظره على صار سبلا (originally حتى صار سنبلا) / جعله في سبيل الله / جففه حتى الحصاد / صنع منه السنابل. جعله at @178 is unmistakably a new option head, so the cut goes at سبلا @177. Med, because I cannot verify the first option's real ending. || ITEM 9, the only item with a stimulus passage, is where all the genuine prose judgement lives. Lead-in ends at عليها @199 (colon, J1). Inside the passage I decline to cut at @210 before عندما: LAW 4 says a trailing عندما adjunct belongs to its main clause, and كما حصل في غزوة أحد modifies يخرجون from inside that same adjunct, so the natural cut is after the whole adjunct complex at أحد @219, immediately before وأمره - which carries a full أن-complement plus ten tokens of new material and so triggers LAW 1 at full strength. I nevertheless add @214 يخرجون at LO confidence, on the single ground that كما حصل في غزوة أحد is comma-set on both sides and B5 says such a span takes two boundaries rather than zero; @214 and @219 stand or fall together, since if the source had no commas there neither exists. @229 الفجر then وفي ذلك إشارة is C4 verbatim: و plus a new topic NP with a nominal predicate. @246 الناس then وذلك حسب قدرته وطاقته is a genuine tension - a four-token tail pulls toward B4 (short tails weld), but C2 (short verdict clauses stand alone, وهو باطل ‖) and the near-certain comma pull the other way; LAW 0 breaks the tie toward cutting, med. || ITEM 10 @271. I explicitly do NOT cut before وأمره بتعلم اللغة العبرية. رأى ... وأمره is a bare V-chain sharing the subject النبي inside a relative clause modifying صحابي, and a cut there would strand هو @276 and its four name options. This is the LAW 1 exception / E2 (فجلس وأكل خبزا وشرب ماء is one segment). Contrast @219 in item 9, where the same وأمره does cut because it heads a full complement clause. The test is arguments, not the letter و. || ITEM 11 @298. ووظيفة كل قسم فيها at @293 is phrase-level و joining two nouns - no cut. But يسمى هذا العلم علم البصريات at @299 introduces a brand-new subject NP, so I cut at العين @298 per C4/LAW 1. Med. || ITEMS 12 AND 17 are the same bet made twice. قوله تعالى @316 and قال تعالى @443 take a colon in essentially every Arabic school text, and LAW 0's corollary says a colon became a ‖. Against this stands G1 (a speech verb welds to its quoted utterance), which cost me five false cuts in batch 1 - but G1 was learned on a translated novel where Arabic dialogue carries no colon at all, and I do not believe it governs a scripture citation in a textbook. I cut both at LO confidence, flagged as a paired gamble. Inside item 17 I do NOT cut at @446 after الأمر, because وشاورهم في الأمر is the grammatical subject of تعود and nothing ends a unit there. || ITEM 13 @373. رحمهم الله is a trailing formulaic du'a covering all four imams. J6's exhortation-tail counter-case governs (gold welds فلنحرص على هذه القيمة), so I weld it into the مسند الامام أحمد option instead of giving it its own segment. This is the one place I consciously overrule LAW 0's cut-at-coin-flip default. || ITEM 14 is a fragment: the question opening was lost at a page break, leaving هو معاوية بن أبي سفيان بن حرب بن أمية وأمه as the visible stem. I cut after وأمه @386 rather than after أمية @385, because all four options are mother-names, which makes وأمه the copular hinge of the stem rather than the head of a new nominal sentence. The بن chains inside the names never cut. Med. || ITEM 15 has the murkiest option boundaries here. بفرض @404 carries a ب that تعزيز @414 does not, which argues for بفرض القانون على الجميع وتحقيق الأمن على النفس والعرض والممتلكات being one option - but that leaves only three options, whereas cutting at الجميع @407 restores the four-option pattern that dominates this bank. The و on وتحقيق does introduce genuinely new arguments (الأمن plus three coordinated PPs), so LAW 1's noun-coordination exception does not shield it. I take the cut at LO per LAW 0's asymmetry. The stem/option-A split at الجناة @403 is med for the same reason. || ITEM 17 @457/@458. I read الشورى and الحرية as separate options and التعاون والتكافل as a fifth, because in this curriculum القيم السياسية are الشورى / العدل والمساواة / الحرية / الطاعة, and التعاون والتكافل is a social value planted as a distractor precisely because it is not political. Five-option items already exist in this document (item 7 has five). || EVERYWHERE ELSE the و and أو inside an option join nouns and never cut: وتحقيق-type pairs, مادية أو معنوية @472, التي تقوي الإنتماء للوطن ومحبته @417-421 (trailing relative, LAW 4), and the whole مثل الرسم والخط والنحت وفن العمارة والتصميم exemplification closing item 20's stem.
